thread.title: Dow Today Drops 260 Points As Caterpillar Weighs; Apple, Visa Up Next | Investor's Business Daily

author: NANCY GONDO
title: Dow Today Drops 260 Points As Caterpillar Weighs; Apple, Visa Up Next | Investor's Business Daily
text:
Stocks remained underwater heading into the last hour of the day's trading session, even though the Dow today, along with other major indexes, trimmed its losses.
X The Dow Jones industrial average was down 1%, after falling as much as 1.7% earlier. The Nasdaq dropped 1.3% and the S&P 500 lost 1%. Small caps fared a little better as the Russell 2000 slid 0.6%. Volume was tracking lower on the NYSE but higher on the Nasdaq vs. the same time Friday.
Caterpillar gapped down and plunged 9% in heavy trade after its Q4 earnings disappointed . The heavy machinery maker, considered a bellwether for the global economy, blamed softer demand in China. Shares tumbled beneath their 50-day moving average and are 24% off their 52-week high.
Caterpillar kicks off a big earnings week for blue chip stocks. Dow components Apple ( AAPL ), Boeing ( BA ), Microsoft ( MSFT ) and Visa ( V ) are all scheduled to report this week.
Among other Dow stocks, Verizon ( VZ ), Visa and Pfizer ( PFE ) each fell more than 2%. Visa, which reports Wednesday after the close , slid below its 50-day line. Apple, which reports Tuesday after the closing bell, was down 1.2%. It's 33% off its January peak and remains below its 50-day and 200-day lines.
Chip, medical and energy stocks were among the biggest sector losers in the stock market today. Airlines, food and building-related stocks bucked the decline.
Chips Fall Hard In Stock Market Today Nvidia ( NVDA ) weighed with a 15% plunge that sent shares gapping down below the 50-day line. The stock is 53% off its 52-week high. The graphics-chip maker, which reports Feb. 14, warned of weaker-than-expected sales for the just-ended fiscal Q4. It expects $2.2 billion in revenue, 18.5% below its prior guidance of $2.7 billion. Nvidia cited "deteriorating macroeconomic conditions, particularly in China."
Other chip designers getting hit included Advanced Micro Devices ( AMD ), down 7%, and Semtech ( SMTC ), which lost 4.5%. VanEck Vectors Semiconductor ETF ( SMH ) and iShares PHLX Semiconductor ETF ( SOXX ) fell more than 2% each.
Medical stocks led the downside in the IBD 50. Drugmaker Horizon Pharma ( HZNP ) sank 4% to breach its 50-day line, while heart-assist device maker Abiomed ( ABMD ) shed nearly 4%. Biotech Regeneron Pharmaceutical ( REGN ) gave up 2%.

Kirkland shares have rallied 15% this year to a record high. The gold miner's stock is well extended from a 23.96 buy point.
CyberArk is flirting with an 81.98 buy point of a cup with handle. The cybersecurity software company, which has a 99 for its Composite and Earnings Per Share ratings, reports Q4 results Feb. 14.
The Innovator IBD 50 ETF ( FFTY ) edged 0.6% lower.
